summary: OpenShift installs use operators with rolling, no-downtime upgrades (with termination_grace_period_seconds), built-in log aggregation and Prometheus/Grafana monitoring; VM-based (RPM) and containerized (Podman with systemd) installs use the playbook installer, halt the platform during upgrades, and need external logging (ELK, Splunk) and monitoring tools.
questions: Can I upgrade AAP without downtime?
How are AAP logs aggregated on VM installs?
Does OpenShift AAP include monitoring dashboards?

answer_card.title: Operations by installation type
answer_card.answer_md:
| Task | OpenShift | VM-based (RPM) | Containerized (Podman) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Install | Operators | Playbook installer, RPMs | Playbook installer, containers under systemd |
| Upgrade | Rolling, no downtime with `termination_grace_period_seconds` | Installer run, platform halted | Installer run, platform halted |
| Logs | Built-in logging stack | External (ELK, Splunk) | External (ELK, Splunk) |
| Monitoring | Built-in Prometheus/Grafana | External tools | External tools |
